description.value: The study examined how salience-network structural integrity and within-network functional connectivity relate to baseline parasympathetic and sympathetic autonomic activity in healthy controls and patients with behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia.

name.value: voxel-based morphometry analysis of baseline RSA

definition.value: smaller gray matter volume was associated with baseline RSA deficits in bvFTD

value: In bvFTD, lower RSA was related to atrophy in a large cluster within the left ventral anterior insula, among other regions.
These findings indicate that structural deterioration of vAI, particularly left vAI, is associated with a loss of basal parasympathetic tone, as measured by RSA.

name.value: voxel-based morphometry analysis of baseline SCL

definition.value: smaller gray matter volume was associated with baseline SCL deficits in bvFTD

value: In bvFTD, smaller volume in inferior temporal gyrus, dorsal mid-insula, and hypothalamus was associated with lower baseline SCL; at more permissive thresholds, smaller volume in the amygdala and PAG was also associated with lower SCL.
These findings suggest that the structural integrity of the right hypothalamus and amygdala is critical for sympathetic outflow and that atrophy in these regions impedes SCL.

spans.text: Volumes were next coregistered to the MPRAGE image and then normalized to the standard MNI-152 healthy adult brain template using SPM segment, producing MNI-registered volumes with 2 mm3 isotropic resolution.

name.value: functional connectivity predictors of baseline RSA

definition.value: functional connectivity strength of salience-network edges was associated with baseline RSA

value: Weaker functional connectivity in bilateral vAI-ACC edges, including left vAI-left ACC, left vAI-right ACC, and right vAI-right ACC, was associated with lower baseline RSA.
Lower RSA was also associated with stronger connectivity between bilateral ACC and predominantly right-sided hypothalamus/amygdala edges.
These findings suggest that RSA depends on both functional integrity of vAI-ACC edges and suppressed connectivity in ACC-hypothalamus and ACC-amygdala edges.

spans.text: Volumes were next coregistered to the MPRAGE image and then normalized to the standard MNI-152 healthy adult brain template using SPM segment, producing MNI-registered volumes with 2 mm3 isotropic resolution.

name.value: functional connectivity predictors of baseline SCL

definition.value: functional connectivity strength of salience-network edges was associated with baseline SCL

value: Stronger bilateral ACC-hypothalamus connectivity was associated with higher baseline SCL, whereas stronger connectivity in bilateral dAI-PAG and left anterior midcingulate cortex-right hypothalamus edges was associated with lower SCL.

Together, these findings suggest that the right hypothalamus in particular is a key hub in sympathetic outflow and that atrophy and diminished connectivity in right hypothalamus/amygdala edges impede SCL.
